Top 3 REITs to Watch This Week
article:
Most
real estate investment trust
(REIT) investors read results the same way.
They find the distribution per unit (DPU), check whether it went up and move on.
That habit can mislead.
Three Singapore REITs report later this month, and each gave investors a reason to read past the headline last time.
Frasers Centrepoint Trust
(SGX: J69U), or FCT, and
Suntec REIT
(SGX: T82U) report on 22 October 2026.
CapitaLand China Trust
(SGX: AU8U), or CLCT, follows on 23 October.
What will FCT’s first financial figures since the half-year reveal?
FCT
is the largest owner of suburban retail space in Singapore.
It owns nine malls and one office property, with assets under management (AUM) of S$8.4 billion.
The manager reports financial figures only at the half-year and full-year marks.
Its business update for the third quarter of FY2026, released on 27 July 2026, carried no net property income (NPI) or DPU.
Retail committed occupancy stood at 99.6% as at 30 June 2026, down from 99.8% three months earlier.
The latest figure excluded Hougang Mall and NEX, both undergoing asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs).
The Hougang Mall AEI was over 98% committed and on track for completion in September 2026, while NEX’s Phase 1 had reached 87% pre-commitment.
Watch how occupancy moves once these malls return to the count.
Shopper traffic rose 2.4% year on year (YoY) in the quarter.
Tenancy churn and refresh held tenants’ sales growth to 0.2%.
FCT did not disclose rental reversion, so look for that figure in the full-year release.
Aggregate leverage stood at 40.4%.
The average cost of debt fell to 3.0% from 3.2% in the preceding quarter.
FCT also proposed to divest White Sands for S$467.0 million, an 8.4% premium to valuation.
The manager earmarked net proceeds of S$454.1 million for debt repayment, which would lower pro forma leverage to 36.5%.
On the flip side, FCT would give up White Sands’ rental income.
Investors should weigh the interest saved against the income lost.
FCT has a 50% interest in the commercial component of a consortium bid for the Bayshore Drive site at a tender price of S$2.1 billion.
Any funding details will shape where leverage goes next.
Related articles:
CICT, FCT or Mapletree Industrial Trust: Which REIT Is the Best Buy Today?
Frasers Property’s Capital Recycling: What It Means for FCT and FLCT
Can Suntec REIT’s DPU growth outlast its one-offs?
Suntec REIT is Singapore’s first composite REIT and owns 10 properties across Singapore, Australia and the UK, with AUM of S$12.2 billion.
For the first half of 2026 (1H2026), DPU rose 24.8% YoY to S$0.039.
Gross revenue grew 1.9% to S$238.9 million, but NPI slipped 0.3% to S$159.0 million.
In other words, DPU grew far faster than property income.
The manager credited stronger Singapore office and retail performance.
A S$9.4 million reduction in financing costs also helped, as did the absence of a S$3.4 million Australian withholding tax provision.
That last item reflects a prior-year comparison, not an operational gain.
Committed occupancy for both Singapore office and retail stood at 99.5% as at 30 June 2026.
Rental reversion came in at 10.1% for office and 10.7% for retail.
Aggregate leverage rose to 43.0%, the highest of the three REITs here.
On 22 October, check whether NPI returns to growth and whether Singapore reversions stay positive.
If the release includes DPU, compare its growth with NPI before reading too much into it.
Related articles:
REITs Underperforming in 2026 vs STI – Is It Time to Buy?
Suntec REIT vs MPACT: Which Offers Better Value for Investors?
When will CLCT’s same-store gains show up in the headline?
CLCT is the largest China-focused Singapore REIT.
It owns 17 properties in China across retail malls, business parks and logistics parks, with AUM of S$4.6 billion.
Its 1H2026 headline numbers looked weak.
Gross revenue fell 5.2% YoY to RMB822.6 million.
NPI declined 3.3% to RMB561.0 million and DPU slipped 1.6% to S$0.0245.
Exclude CapitaMall Yuhuating, which CLCT divested in October 2025, and the picture improves.
On that same-store basis, revenue eased only 0.2%.
NPI grew 1.3% and DPU rose 2.9%.
The Yuhuating drag should fade once YoY comparisons move past the divestment.
Business parks remain the weak spot.
Committed occupancy fell to 85.1% from 86.9% a year ago, with rental reversion at -12.0%.
Retail reversion stood at -2.7%, though retail occupancy improved to 97.3% from 96.9%.
Logistics shows the most encouraging trend.
Occupancy rose to 99.0% from 96.6%.
Reversion improved to -1.2% in 1H2026 from -24.5% for the full FY2025.
The periods differ, but a move into positive territory would be worth noting.
CLCT also saved 16% on interest YoY.
Aggregate leverage improved to 40.4% from 42.1%, with the average cost of debt at 3.06%.
A higher realised foreign exchange loss offset part of these gains, so watch the
currency line
on 23 October.
Related articles:
3 High-Yielding REITs Paying Over 6.5%: Bargains or Traps?
3 Singapore REITs, 3 Different Stories: What the FY2025 Results Really Tell Us
Get Smart: Find what filled the gap
DPU tells you what unitholders received.
NPI tells you what the properties earned.
When the two move apart, find out why before deciding whether the trend will last.
When these three REITs report, put the DPU change next to the NPI change.
If the gap is wide, look for the bridge.
Interest savings and one-off items can lift DPU growth above NPI growth for a while.
Then, ask the really important question: ask whether that bridge will still be there next year.

title: US stock futures rise ahead of busy earnings week
article:
(Oct 19) : US stock futures rose and oil edged lower as traders prepared for a packed week of corporate earnings and Chinese economic data against a backdrop of heightened geopolitical risks.

Futures on the S&P 500 Index advanced, erasing earlier losses after the underlying gauge fell 1.1% Friday, capping its worst week since June. The VIX Index jumped to a four-month intraday high on Friday as technology shares slumped, while the dollar was mixed against major peers in early trading.

More than 70 S&P 500 companies are due to report this week, including Magnificent Seven members Tesla Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc., putting the durability of the artificial-intelligence trade back in the spotlight. In Asia, a swath of Chinese economic data Monday will offer fresh clues on the health of the world’s second-largest economy.

Brent crude fell 0.7% after climbing Friday, with oil near US$110 a barrel adding to inflation concerns and complicating the outlook for interest rates. The Federal Reserve has entered its communications blackout period ahead of its Oct. 28 policy decision, while geopolitical risks remained elevated as relations between the US and Ukraine deteriorated.

Investors are bracing for further swings across stocks and bonds as questions grow over whether massive spending on AI infrastructure will deliver sufficient returns. A measure of bond volatility also remains elevated, while persistent fuel and food inflation is adding pressure on central banks.

We’re in “a classic period of heightened uncertainty,” said Kyle Rodda, a senior analyst at Capital.com in Melbourne. “Several things are colliding at the same time. AI earnings are coming up, interest rate uncertainty is persistent and the midterms are a few weeks away. For Asia, the impacts will be more acute given that all of these themes are amplified because of exposure to chips, higher yields and energy prices.”

See also: MSCI weighs downgrade of Indonesia to remove from global indexes

Treasuries, which had been favored as a haven during the technology selloff, came under pressure Friday as oil climbed. Brent rose at the end of last week on doubts over US President Donald Trump’s deal to release more Russian diesel into global markets and supply disruptions stretching from the Strait of Hormuz to the Black Sea.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia, escalating a week-long row with the US president.

“I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table. Great progress is being made,” Trump wrote in a social-media post.

See also: Stock buyers step in to power Wall Street rebound

Elsewhere, the euro lagged major peers as protests in several French cities descended into clashes between police and demonstrators, with looting and landmarks set on fire. Demonstrations also took place in Belgium, Italy and Portugal.

Chinese assets will be closely watched after authorities moved last week to shore up the equity market by urging companies and state funds to buy shares and guiding some investors to curb selling. The measures followed a technology-driven slump that sent the CSI 300 Index to its lowest since August 2025.

Monday’s data, including third-quarter gross domestic product, will provide fresh clues on China’s outlook. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect growth to rebound slightly, though weak consumption, sluggish private investment and a prolonged property downturn remain drags.

Investors will also look for signs of additional policy support as top financial officials, including People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, speak at the 2026 Financial Street Forum starting Monday. Easing bets have increased, with China’s one-year interest-rate swap falling last week to its lowest since April 2020.

“We expect a continuation of the ‘two-speed economy’ of strong industrial production for exports and weak growth in domestic demand,” Commonwealth Bank of Australia strategists led by Joseph Capurso wrote in a note.
